correctness.rationale: For size-k committee with cut b, degree counting gives inside=outside=(n-b)/2; hence CC grand score (n+b)/2 and PAV grand score (3n+b)/4. For each candidate, its d incident voters can deviate with one seat and require total payment >=d. Summing over vertices forces total transfers >=n. Uniform per-edge-voter payment 1 stably dominates every coalition since its score is <= number of selected endpoint incidences <=d floor(|S|/d)<=|S|. Thus subsidy equals n minus grand value. B(H)=n exactly for bipartite d-regular H, with equal sides in each component. Independent full regular-graph enumeration to 6 vertices and selected all-coalition checks agreed.

value.rationale: An explicit equality connects a central graph optimization problem (balanced maximum cut) to the exact stabilization subsidy of a natural TU approval election, with a uniform optimal allocation and sharp bipartiteness criterion. It is not a mere restatement of the prior K4 counterexample.

final_claim: For any nonempty simple d-regular H on 2k vertices, one edge-approval voter per edge, half-vertex committee, and TU CC or PAV: CoS_CC=(n-B(H))/2 and CoS_PAV=(n-B(H))/4 with n=kd and B(H) maximum balanced bisection; uniform voter payment 1 attains optimum; no-subsidy TU core iff H is bipartite.
